classification: Missing-transaction callback exposed when custom purchase logic was added.
evidence: This PR changed the native event builder to omit a nil transaction and added the supported custom-success path. Its unchanged TypeScript declaration still required `storeTransaction`. Historical native/JS boundary execution produces `undefined`, accepts an unguarded typed consumer, and then throws `TypeError`. The required TypeScript declaration dates back to [#887](https://github.com/RevenueCat/react-native-purchases/pull/887) (`a8a84f8d340bddd46c72b137f3dd498601ded7b5`, 2024-02-14), despite an already-optional native delegate contract. Injecting nil into that older implementation throws natively instead of delivering this callback. Thus #887 introduced the type-contract mismatch; #1607 introduced the reported missing-field/custom-purchase case.
limitations: Historical method bodies, callback expressions and property types were executed in isolation. The then-pinned iOS 5.59.2 custom-success nil result was source-checked; its complete purchase flow was not rerun.
